$comment: How the BDD-only mutation run (config/mutation/stryker.bdd.config.mjs) is split across jobs. One unsharded run mutates every file in src/ against the BDD suite alone and does not finish: its first and only attempt was killed at 30 minutes (nightly-mutation.yml, 2026-09-17), so config/mutation/bdd-thresholds.json could not be seeded until the sharded run first completed (2026-09-19). Each shard here is a set of directories; nightly-mutation.yml runs one job per shard and merges the reports before the ratchet, so the gate still sees one score per directory.
$invariant: The shards partition src/: every TypeScript file under it belongs to exactly one shard. src/sde has its own shard (Track S Run 2) so its directories are scored, ratcheted and restored on their own. tests/tdd/mutation-ratchet/bddShards.test.ts fails on a file claimed twice or not at all, so a shard boundary cannot quietly drop a directory from the run. The exclusions in config/mutation/stryker.bdd.config.mjs apply to every shard alike, so the union of the shards mutates exactly what the unsharded glob did.
$balance: Balanced on 2026-10-07 so each shard should finish inside 30 minutes, because GitHub reclaims long-running runners ("The runner has received a shutdown signal") often enough that the 37-138 minute shards before it lost one most nights. Method: Stryker's instrumenter counted each file's mutants (StringLiteral excluded, as in stryker.bdd.config.mjs), each file was weighted by its old shard's observed minutes per mutant (2026-10-04 to 10-07 nightlies: core 10-15 per 100, rest 11, sde 4.4, clients 2.5, schemas 1.6), and the files were packed into shards of about 22 minutes. A heavy file gets a shard of its own. Each original area keeps its old name as the catch-all shard: it includes the area's directories and excludes what the split-out shards claim, so a new file lands in it rather than in no shard. Known over budget: src/core/rateLimiter/RateLimiter.ts alone (402 mutants, estimated 54 minutes) is the core-rate-limiter shard; one file cannot be split by directory, so it stays a single long shard. Re-balance from the job durations in nightly-mutation.yml when a shard drifts past 30 minutes. A shard may set `concurrency` below the default 6 when its runner runs out of memory: core-root-1 and core-request-pipeline were killed every night from 2026-10-05 (SIGKILL in Stryker's child processes, 15-51 minutes in, #587) and run 3 test runners. core-rate-limiter joined them on 2026-10-13: after passing in 51-61 minutes every night to 2026-10-12, both attempts on 2026-10-13 lost their runner 23 and 37 minutes in, with the progress line stalling and the 10-second log cadence slipping first (#650), while core-request-pipeline ran 55 minutes at 3 runners without a loss. core-status-handling, core-middleware and core-etag-cache joined them on 2026-10-18 (#670): all three lost their runner on the first attempt (24-40 minutes in) and the first two again on the retry (15 and 30 minutes in), each while timed-out mutants piled up, on the night the four shards already at 3 runners passed. At 6 runners they took 21-38 minutes on green nights, so 3 runners keeps them near an hour at worst. core-pagination joined them on 2026-10-23 (#670): it lost its runner on the retry three nights running (2026-10-21 to 10-23, 21-70 minutes in), again while timed-out mutants piled up. The same nights several shards failed in 5 minutes instead; that was Stryker's dry-run timeout, not memory, and stryker.bdd.config.mjs now allows the initial test run 20 minutes.
